title: The actual completion unit on every simultaneous quotient presentation
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E/Q_l and a scheme X with l invertible in every residue field. There exist a derived quotient-system calculus S and a normalized natural Roos model r such that for every flat-term K-flat complex P and whole-system adjunction-coherent simultaneous quotient presentation (C,e,kappa), in the sense of IsIntegralComparisonPresentationCoherent from [def-trf-integral-comparison-realization-models], the actual S adjunction unit followed by realization of e and the fixed Roos comparison is the localization of a chain map v. The nth unshifted product component of v sends x to the canonical restricted system section corresponding to kappa_n inverse of 1 tensor x; all shifted product components vanish. No completeness, boundedness or constructibility hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tags 03EK, 07A6, 09T5, 0D6E and 0941; actual-unit normalization transported along the strict simultaneous quotient tower comparison, as in the recorded strict-quotient-completion-unit and isomorphism-multiplication-cone-descent refinements.

proof.text: Choose the compatible canonical models S, M and D. Use the existing proved private roosModel of the isomorphism-derived-pullback normalization module: its comparison is D.roos inverse, with K-injective normalization proved there.

Apply strictQuotientCompletionRealization directly to S and r to obtain rho. For the given whole-system coherent presentation, its normalization supplies the strict tower isomorphism a and the entire derived equation for rho. This uses the coherent hypothesis and never infers equality of a derived map from finite evaluations.

Let b be the actual strict quotient cone augmentation and set v=b followed by H(a inverse). The proved normalized_tower_map helper identifies a_n with the canonical restriction/evaluation comparison followed by Res(kappa_n). Cancel its two isomorphisms to obtain the inverse equation. After the nth product projection, the proved Roos coordinate formula reduces v to the quotient unit followed by a_n inverse. unrestrictedTowerUnit_condition gives 1 tensor x and restricted_section_cancel cancels the canonical section casts. The second Roos coordinate is zero since the strict augmentation has zero shifted coordinate and the Roos map is diagonal.

Postcompose the desired derived equality with Q(H(a hom)). The normalization of rho makes the left side the actual unit followed by rho; the inverse identities make the right side Q(b). Apply strictQuotientCompletionUnit, using that the fixed r is D.roos inverse, and cancel the isomorphism. The same construction includes zero complexes and empty sites with no boundedness or completeness condition.

theorem effectiveCompletionPresentationModels
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E]
    [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E] (X : Scheme.{t})
    [∀ x : X, Invertible (l : X.residueField x)] :
    ∃ (S : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l E X)
      (ρ : IntegralComparisonRoosModel l E X),
    ∀ (P : (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E X).FullSubcategory)
    (C : CochainComplex (coefficientSequenceModules l E X) ℤ)
    (e : S.reduction.obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P.obj) ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj C)
    (κ : ∀ n : ℕ,
      ((coefficientSequenceEvaluation l E X n).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj C ≅
        (unrestrictedIntegralFiniteComplex l E X n).obj P.obj),
    CoefficientReductionPresentation l E X S.toCoefficientDerivedSystemReduction
      P.obj P.property.1 C e κ →
    IsIntegralComparisonPresentationCoherent l E X S P.obj C e κ →
    ∃ v : P.obj ⟶ integralOperationsRoos
        (((coefficientSequenceRestriction l E X).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj C).asFunctor,
      (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : ℤ) (U : X.ProEtᵒᵖ) (x : (P.obj.X i).val.obj U),
        (((v ≫ CochainComplex.mappingCocone.fst (scalarRoosBoundary
          (((coefficientSequenceRestriction l E X).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
            C).asFunctor) ≫ Pi.π (fun m ↦
              ((((coefficientSequenceRestriction l E X).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
                C).asFunctor.obj (op m))) n).f i).val.app U) x =
          integralComparisonRestrictedSection l E X (C.X i) n U
            (integralComparisonSequenceSection l E X (C.X i) n U
              (((κ n).inv.f i).val.app U
                (unrestrictedIntegralTensorSection l E X n (P.obj.X i) U 1 x)))) ∧
      (∀ (i j : ℤ) (h : i + -1 = j), v.f i ≫
        (CochainComplex.mappingCocone.snd (scalarRoosBoundary
          (((coefficientSequenceRestriction l E X).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
            C).asFunctor)).v i j h = 0) ∧
      S.adjunction.unit.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P.obj) ≫
        (coefficientSequenceLimit l E X).map e.hom ≫
        (integralComparisonRoosBridge l E X ρ C).hom = DerivedCategory.Q.map v

old_proof.text: Choose compatible canonical ordinary and derived completion models. The existing proved private inverse Roos model from the isomorphism-derived-pullback-comparison normalization module has the requisite K-injective normalization. Apply multiplication-cone descent to the identity scheme map to obtain a normalized representative completion comparison rho. For a presentation C let a identify its restricted tower with the strict quotient tower of P. Transport the strict quotient cone augmentation b by H(a inverse). Its product components are the quotient units transported by kappa inverse; its shifted components vanish because the Roos map preserves the two coordinates diagonally. Postcompose the derived identity with Q(H(a)): rho normalization and the strict quotient completion unit theorem identify both sides with Q(b). Cancel the isomorphism. The argument also applies to the zero complex.
